annotationRationale: The stopping rule identifies a complete family of disjoint successful histories. Independence gives their probabilities, which sum as a convergent geometric series.
sourceMethod: Follows the official method of listing alternating successful histories and summing their probabilities. The explanation justifies why the list is exhaustive and contains no overlapping events.

review.mathCheck: Before stopping, flips alternate. Success requires starting THT and then ending at the first HH, so the successful histories are exactly (TH)^nH for n≥2. Their disjoint probabilities sum to (1/32)/(1-1/4)=1/24, choice B, matching the key. Every listed history respects the stopping rule.
review.sourceMethodCheck: The attached MAA solution 21 lists the identical successful histories and sums their probabilities with ratio 1/4. The candidate provides an originally worded, faithful adaptation with additional justification of completeness and mutual exclusivity.
review.annotationCheck: Infinite geometric summation and addition of disjoint probabilities are appropriate assessed concepts; independent-flip probability is appropriate support. The derivation is reconstructible at AMC 10 level. No recursion or conditional-probability replacement is needed.
